subject: Science
title: Show what we know
objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
content: Revising the body and senses, water, sand and soil, and weather through play stations and gathering Term 1 evidence.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and playful; observe quietly and record without interrupting; offer help only when a child is stuck; celebrate what each child can do.
learnerActivities: Show what they know about the body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather through play.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 1 science learning using the four-level scale.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.

lessons.title: Revising my body and senses
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit body parts and the five senses through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored their body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather this term.
lessons.starter: Sing the body song and say "Today we play our favourite body and senses games."
teacherActivities: Sing the body song and touch each part.
Play the mystery bag game with touch.
Show the five sense cards and ask "Which sense?"
Let each child choose a favourite game.
learnerActivities: Child points to the body part.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing the body song and touch each part. Children: Children touch each part.
Step 2. Teacher: Play the mystery bag game with touch. Children: Child feels and guesses.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the five sense cards and ask "Which sense?" Children: Child points to the body part.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Body and senses games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
The teacher notes who names parts and senses.
practical.safety: Use safe objects only and keep floors clear. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use three body parts.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the body song quietly and sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Play body and senses games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit body parts and the five senses through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising water, sand and soil
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit water, sand and soil through play.
successCriteria: Plays with water, sand and soil safely
Says wet, dry, float or sink
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored their body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather this term.
resources: Trays of wet and dry sand
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play with water, sand and soil." Show the three areas.
teacherActivities: Play float and sink with the water basin.
Dig in the sand and soil.
Let each child choose a favourite play area.
learnerActivities: Children put objects in the water.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play float and sink with the water basin. Children: Children put objects in the water.
Step 2. Teacher: Dig in the sand and soil. Children: Children dig and scoop.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare wet and dry sand. Children: Child says wet or dry.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite play area. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Earth and water play
steps: The teacher notes words and actions.
practical.safety: Supervise each area closely. Keep water shallow and wash hands after play.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and name what they do.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to explain float and sink to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the sand wet or dry?

expectedOutcomes: Plays safely with water, sand and soil
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Play with water, sand and soil at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit water, sand and soil through play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising weather
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit weather words and dressing for the weather.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored their body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather this term.
lessons.starter: Look out of the window together and say "What is the weather today?"
teacherActivities: Look at the sky and name the weather.
Put the picture on the weather chart.
Choose clothes for the weather and dress the doll.
Play with streamers or an umbrella.
learnerActivities: Child plays and says wind or rain.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Look at the sky and name the weather. Children: Children say the weather.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the picture on the weather chart. Children: Child places the picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Choose clothes for the weather and dress the doll. Children: Child chooses clothes.
Step 4. Teacher: Play with streamers or an umbrella. Children: Child plays and says wind or rain.

practical.title: Weather games
steps: Set up the weather chart and clothes.
Children name the weather and choose clothes.
practical.safety: Stay in safe areas and watch for weather hazards. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say the weather.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what to wear.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names the weather with a word
lessons.conclusion: Sing the weather song and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about the weather each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit weather words and dressing for the weather" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Science play stations
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 science learning at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows body, senses, water and weather knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored their body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather this term.
lessons.starter: Sing the body song and show six stations to the class.
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Six stations
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep water shallow and floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names body parts; uses senses; plays with water; says wet or dry; names the weather.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite science game at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 science learning at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: Term 1 science celebration
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 1 with songs, experiments and games, and teachers will complete their records.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored their body, senses, water, sand, soil and weather this term.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate. Let us sing and play our favourite science games."
teacherActivities: Play float and sink as a class.
Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name.
learnerActivities: Children join in and choose a song.
Child puts an object in the water and says float or sink.
Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs with actions. Children: Children join in and choose a song.
Step 2. Teacher: Play float and sink as a class. Children: Child puts an object in the water and says float or sink.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sing, play float and sink and say each name.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Keep water shallow and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing along.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 1 science record using today’s observations and the week’s notes. Record a next step for Term 2.

questions.question: Did you like it?
questions.expected: Yes with a smile or word.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Term 2."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep exploring at home during the holiday and talk about what you notice.
